newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank offers one-day rrp at 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank offers one-day rrp at 13 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it started offering one-day reverse repos at a rate of 13 percent.
Philippine Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said this effectively raises the overnight borrowing rate to 13 from 12 percent.
This is the second time in a day the Central Bank has had to raise its key rate as a pre-emptive move to quell peso speculation.
Early in the day, the Central Bank lifted its rate by 75 basis points to 12 percent.
"We just want to send the message across that we mean business...Even if we don't see any action, we just want to pre-empt the market," Edeza said.
The Central Bank feared the peso may come under attack from the backlash of the problems of the Thai baht.
Edeza said the Central Bank was both a seller and a buyer of dollars today. "It's not a big amount. We cannot say it's an intervention amount."
The peso had traded from 26.275/26.372 with volume heavy at $259 million in late trades.
